name: Salem State University

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility bound to MA's legally mandated 50% by 2030 / net-zero by 2050 emissions targets (Next-Generation Roadmap Act)

fundingAttached.note: Named recipient of a $7.5M DCAMM Leading by Example grant (shared with Mass Maritime) for geothermal phase 1 — real dollar figure, not just a pledge

confirmation.note: Confirmed via official Mass.gov press release naming SSU directly

flagNote: Named alongside Mass Maritime in a confirmed $7.5M state decarbonization grant — legal mandate plus funding already attached, not just a voluntary pledge.

financial.text: DCAMM awarded $7.5M to support large-scale geothermal projects at Massachusetts Maritime Academy and Salem State University, funding first-phase work connecting several buildings on each campus to a geothermal system.
financial.source: Mass.gov press release, Executive Office of Energy and Environmental Affairs / DOER

name: Massachusetts Maritime Academy

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility, same MA net-zero/2030 legal mandate as other public MA colleges

fundingAttached.note: Named recipient of the same $7.5M DCAMM grant (shared with Salem State) for geothermal phase 1

confirmation.note: Confirmed via official Mass.gov press release naming MMA directly

flagNote: A specialized, low-profile public academy landing real decarbonization construction funding — exactly the kind of school a prestige-only screen would miss.

financial.text: DCAMM awarded $7.5M (shared with Salem State) to connect campus buildings to new geothermal systems, laying groundwork for further decarbonization; expected to cut on-site fossil fuel emissions at both schools combined by at least 50%.
financial.source: Mass.gov press release, Executive Office of Energy and Environmental Affairs / DOER

name: University of Massachusetts Boston

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility bound to MA net-zero mandate; also subject to Boston's BERDO ordinance as a Boston-located institution

deadlineProximity.note: Chancellor states the project will beat both the 2030 and 2040 state targets ahead of schedule

fundingAttached.note: Confirmed $5.3M DIG grant, funding replacement of central plant gas boilers with electric heat-shift chillers

confirmation.note: Confirmed via Mass.gov press release plus an on-record Chancellor quote

flagNote: One of the three schools the original brief specifically named as a real anti-prestige signal — real funded construction, not a pledge.

financial.text: Awarded $5.3M to fund the initial phases of a campus-wide decarbonization plan, replacing central power plant natural gas boilers with three electric heat-shift chillers; expected to cut Central Utility Plant natural gas use by ~82%, ahead of the Commonwealth's 2030/2040 targets per the Chancellor's own statement.
financial.source: Mass.gov press release, Executive Office of Energy and Environmental Affairs / DOER

name: Emerson College

mandateStrength.note: Voluntary carbon-neutral-by-2030 institutional pledge, but also legally covered by Boston's BERDO ordinance (binding emissions caps + daily fines for large buildings)

fundingAttached.note: No public grant dollar figure — decarbonization funded via a private energy-service partnership (Vicinity Energy eSteam), not a disclosed capital number

confirmation.note: Confirmed via Higher Ed Dive reporting and Emerson/Vicinity's own published case study

flagNote: A small, urban, non-flagship private college moving first on a named decarbonization technology to hit both its own pledge and BERDO's legal deadlines.

financial.text: Partnered with Vicinity Energy to convert to "eSteam," a carbon-free district steam product, aiming to decarbonize 100% of campus heating — positioned explicitly as a way to meet both Emerson's 2030 carbon-neutral pledge and Boston's BERDO emissions requirements. No public capital cost figure disclosed for the conversion itself.
financial.source: Higher Ed Dive; Vicinity Energy customer case study
financial.asOf: Jul 2024 (Higher Ed Dive); Nov 2025 (Vicinity case study)

name: Quinsigamond Community College

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility, same MA net-zero legal mandate

fundingAttached.note: Early-stage: a $25,600 state feasibility study grant for a large-scale solar canopy + battery storage — real state money, but pre-construction, not a build yet

confirmation.note: Confirmed via official Mass.gov Leading by Example grant records

flagNote: Currently at the feasibility-study stage for a large solar canopy project — an early, pre-construction signal worth tracking as the study concludes.

financial.text: Awarded a $25,600 Leading by Example feasibility study grant (2020) to assess a large-scale solar canopy with battery storage at its Worcester campus, including the impact of interconnecting the system.
financial.source: Mass.gov, Leading by Example Awarded Grant Descriptions

name: Roxbury Community College

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility bound to MA net-zero mandate; Boston location also brings BERDO exposure

fundingAttached.note: 937 kW solar canopy already completed (2016) as part of a larger DCAMM energy project, ~$5.3M in projected 20-year energy cost savings — a completed project, not a pending one, so read as a track record rather than an active near-term build

confirmation.note: Confirmed via official Mass.gov Leading by Example grant records

flagNote: A small Boston-based community college already carrying a completed large-scale solar project — a track record of using state decarbonization funding for real construction.

financial.text: A 937 kW solar canopy over the college's Parking Lot No. 1, completed in 2016 as part of a larger DCAMM energy project, projected to cut GHG emissions by 369 metric tons/year and reduce energy costs by an estimated $5.3M over 20 years.
financial.source: Mass.gov, Leading by Example Awarded Grant Descriptions

name: Berkshire Community College

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility, same MA net-zero legal mandate

fundingAttached.note: Recognized for solar PV generating ~20% of campus electricity; no new dollar figure disclosed in this recognition for a pending project

confirmation.note: Confirmed via official 2019 Mass.gov Leading by Example Awards press release

flagNote: A small Berkshires public college with an already-strong sustainability record (81% waste diversion, 2nd nationally in Recyclemania) — a credible compliance-minded client, not yet tied to a new dollar figure.

financial.text: Recognized at the 2019 Leading by Example Awards for solar PV generating the equivalent of ~20% of campus electricity consumption, an 81% waste diversion rate, and other sustainability initiatives.
financial.source: Mass.gov, 2019 Leading by Example Awards press release

name: Massasoit Community College

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility, same MA net-zero legal mandate

deadlineProximity.note: 2030 interim target, though the underlying project is now over a decade old

fundingAttached.note: A completed, large DCAMM-led energy/water conservation retrofit projected to save $12M over 20 years and cut energy use 40% — real dollar scale, but historical, not a current pending project

confirmation.note: Confirmed via official Mass.gov Leading by Example award record

flagNote: One of the largest verified dollar-savings figures in this list ($12M/20yr) — dated, but shows the school has a real track record of major DCAMM-partnered capital retrofits.

financial.text: Under the leadership of a former VP of Administration/CFO (2007–2012), Massasoit completed a comprehensive energy and water conservation project with DCAMM, projected to cut energy use 40% and save $12M over 20 years; also installed 370 kW of solar PV across five campus buildings.
financial.source: Mass.gov, 2012 Leading by Example Award Winners

name: Cape Cod Community College

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility, same MA net-zero legal mandate

fundingAttached.note: Confirmed $170,000 state grant for a 635 kW solar canopy, plus an already-built zero-net-energy science building

confirmation.note: Confirmed via the college's own news release and independent local reporting (CapeCod.com)

flagNote: Only community college recognized at the 2022 statewide Leading by Example awards — a 67% emissions cut since 2004 and an active, newly-funded solar canopy project.

financial.text: Received a $170,000 state grant for a 635 kW third-party-owned solar canopy at its Lot 12 parking area, alongside its existing net-zero-energy Frank and Maureen Wilkens Science and Engineering Center. Recognized at the 16th Annual Leading by Example Awards for a 67% cut in campus GHG emissions vs. a 2004 baseline.
financial.source: CapeCod.com; Cape Cod Community College news release

name: North Shore Community College

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility, same MA net-zero legal mandate

deadlineProximity.note: 2030 interim target, though the flagship project itself dates to ~2012

fundingAttached.note: Built the first state-owned Zero Net Energy building in Massachusetts (Health Professions and Student Services Building) — a real, large, already-completed construction project

confirmation.note: Confirmed via official Mass.gov Leading by Example award record

flagNote: Holds a genuine state first — the first-ever state-owned Zero Net Energy building — showing an institutional willingness to build ambitiously for compliance, even if the flagship project itself is now over a decade old.

financial.text: Opened the first state-owned Zero Net Energy Building in Massachusetts: the Health Professions and Student Services Building, featuring a 345 kW solar PV system, greywater storage, and a geothermal ground-source heat pump system. Also installed 139 kW of additional solar capacity across its Danvers and Lynn campuses.
financial.source: Mass.gov, 2012 Leading by Example Award Winners

name: Southern Connecticut State University

mandateStrength.note: Charter Second Nature signatory with its own Climate Action Plan; also a CT public university under Gov. Lamont's Executive Order 21-3 (45% emissions cut by 2030, 80% by 2050)

fundingAttached.note: Part of a confirmed 2.32 MW solar project (shared with Gateway Community College) with $6M in projected 20-year savings

confirmation.note: Confirmed via GovTech reporting and SCSU's own published Climate Action Plan

flagNote: Connecticut's first real anti-prestige find — a charter climate-pledge signatory with an actual funded, dollar-figure solar project, not just an aspirational plan.

financial.text: Part of a 2.32 megawatt solar project (with Gateway Community College) estimated to save $6 million over 20 years. SCSU is a charter signatory of the Climate Leadership Commitment and maintains its own Climate Action Plan targeting net carbon neutrality by 2050 at the latest.
financial.source: GovTech; Southern Connecticut State University Climate Action Plan

name: Manchester Community College

mandateStrength.note: Part of Connecticut State Colleges and Universities (CSCU), which has made system-wide carbon neutrality commitments; CT is also under a legal 2030/2040/2050 decarbonization mandate

fundingAttached.note: Confirmed solar installation funded by CT Green Bank, part of a CSCU-wide deal projected to save more than $10M over 20 years; construction beginning

confirmation.note: Confirmed via Hartford Business Journal reporting naming the school directly

flagNote: One of three CSCU schools receiving new solar systems this pass, with two more (CCSU, Western CT State) explicitly slated to follow within two years — a visible near-term pipeline, not a one-off.

financial.text: Selected, alongside Southern Connecticut State University and Middlesex Community College, to receive new solar energy systems through a CSCU partnership with Current (GE), SunLight Solar Energy, and CT Green Bank; construction began fall 2025. The initiative is projected to save CSCU more than $10 million within 20 years, with Central CT State, Western CT State, and others slated to follow.

name: Rhode Island College

mandateStrength.note: State-owned facility under RI's legally binding 2021 Act on Climate (45% emissions reduction below 1990 levels by 2030)

fundingAttached.note: Confirmed $14M, two-year, 41-building infrastructure upgrade — one of the largest specific dollar figures found in this list

confirmation.note: Confirmed via the Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources' own published case study

flagNote: The strongest Rhode Island find — a real, large, multi-building capital project already underway, directly tied to the state's legally binding climate law.

financial.text: Completed the first phase of a two-year, $14 million project to upgrade 41 buildings and campus infrastructure, expected to save more than $1.6 million annually in energy costs for the next 15 years.
financial.source: Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources, "Lead by Example" case study

name: Vermont Technical College (Vermont State University)

mandateStrength.note: Part of the Vermont State Colleges System, a Vermont Clean and Resilient Energy Consortium member; VT's 2020 Global Warming Solutions Act sets legally binding emissions targets

deadlineProximity.note: 2030 interim target (26% below 2005 levels by 2025, 40% below 1990 by 2030)

fundingAttached.note: A named, completed 100-solar-tracker farm producing ~1M kWh/year, plus an on-campus anaerobic digester ("Big Bertha") converting farm waste to renewable electricity and heat — real infrastructure, though the project itself dates to 2020

confirmation.note: Confirmed via Vermont Tech's own announcement and Solar Power World trade coverage

flagNote: Vermont's clearest higher-ed decarbonization example — a real, named renewable energy installation doubling as a teaching lab, at a small technical college most outsiders wouldn't think to check.

financial.text: Operates a 100-unit AllEarth Renewables solar tracker array (in operation since Feb 2020) projected to produce nearly 1 million kWh annually, plus an anaerobic digester ("Big Bertha") converting farm manure and food waste into renewable electricity and heat for the college.
financial.source: Vermont Technical College announcement; Solar Power World

name: University of Southern Maine

mandateStrength.note: Part of the University of Maine System; Maine's 2019 climate law sets a legally binding 45% emissions cut below 1990 levels by 2030

fundingAttached.note: Three existing campus solar systems, geothermal heat pumps on two buildings, and a new residence hall on track to be the 2nd-largest Passive House-certified university building in the US — real, specific, but no single new dollar figure disclosed

confirmation.note: Confirmed via USM's own official sustainability page

flagNote: Maine's strongest non-flagship find — a specific, named Passive House residence hall project, not just a general pledge.

financial.text: Operates three solar systems across its Gorham and Portland campuses; the Abromson and Wishcamper buildings are heated and cooled by geothermal heat pumps. A new Portland residence hall is on track to become the second-largest Passive House-certified university building in the United States.
financial.source: University of Southern Maine, official sustainability page

name: Plymouth State University

mandateStrength.note: New Hampshire has no legally binding state climate mandate (unlike the other five New England states) — PSU's push is a voluntary 2009 institutional pledge (ACUPCC), not law. Scored much lower than other schools on this list for that reason

fundingAttached.note: A named, real solar array (PE Center) exists, but no disclosed dollar figure and no legal deadline forcing action

confirmation.note: Confirmed via Green Energy Times reporting and PSU's own sustainability office statements

flagNote: Included for genuine New England-wide coverage, but honestly the weakest mandate case on this list — New Hampshire has no binding state climate law, so this is a voluntary institutional commitment, not a legal pressure point. Worth keeping visible, but with appropriately tempered expectations.

financial.text: Installed a solar array at its Physical Education Center as part of a Climate Action Plan (2010) targeting 50% emissions reduction by 2025 and full carbon neutrality by 2050, with a nearer-term goal of carbon-neutral electricity by 2030. PSU was a charter signatory of the American College & University Presidents' Climate Commitment in 2009.
financial.source: Green Energy Times; Plymouth State University Office of Environmental Sustainability
